A Neural Network

Imagine you are given many pictures of faces (48 Million pixels), and you’re asked to identify one of 1000 possible people. 
Imagine you are given speech waves and you’re asked to to identify for each, which of 25 sounds each speech wave corresponds to.
What can do this? A Neural Network (NN)
I will not tell you now why it’s called a NN. I will teach you what it is by what it does– how it walks and how it swims.
The job of an NN is to take a bunch of numbers the 48M pixels in one image/numbers of a wave and to return a probability distribution.
For speech the probability distribution is 25 sounds
But let’s say it had just 5 vowels, this is a pdf: [.2,.2,.4,.2,0]
And let’s say we agree the vowel order is read, rad, rude, Rud, rod
The p’s must sum to 1 (100%)
That says: there’s 20% chance the sound is the v in read, 20% it’s the vowel in rad, 40% the vowel in rude, 20% it’s the vowel in Rud, and 0% it’s the vowel in Rod.
A Neural Network

The input of an NN is a bunch of numbers, signal, or a vector, e.g., [4,1,-3,2,1,.4,1,2,-3,…] (usually 1000’s of nums). Let’s say these are the pressure numbers of a speech wave
The output of the NN is a decision pdf: Given the signal, what’s the p(each object): p of each vowels read, rad, rude, Rud, rod 
How? How can NNs do that? How can it make a decision.
They have knowledge, in a bunch of weights w’s
And somehow the input signal vector is combined with these w’s and a decision about the object detected is made, eventually, as there are many many w’s and many many calculations! Several trillion w’s and billions of calculations.
These magical w’s allow the NN to make decisions, but how does it know these w’s???
Fake it till you make it!
SGD for NNs. You start out with random w’s.
Give it a signal (let’s say we give it the vowel in Rud)
Forward Propagation: It uses its stupid w’s, and it produces a pdf that doesn’t reflect reality: [.4,.1,.2,.2,.1]
We tell it: NO!!!!!!! You should have decided: 0,0,0,1,0], so it realizes it made a big Error or Loss
It improves its w’s to reduce the Loss
Give it another signal and repeat billions of times!
But what calculations are actullay made on the signal???
Templatic Perception and Hierarchical Perception

Our Goal: Understand how an NN uses its weights to process the input to make the right decision at the output, e.g., when given a [z] speech signal (= waveform = pressure waveform), the correct decision should be [z], not [s], not [a], etc.
Something useful to know is how humans perceive speech, faces, etc. And perhaps knowing how how our own biological neural networks perceive speech, we can use that to understand how NNs model this via an artificial computation.
So there are two basic theories of animal perception that inform NN design:
Templatic Perception
Hierarchical Perception
Templatic Perception

Here’s a theory of how face perception works
The retina in the eye receives light information from the face
The brain has a template, a picture of sorts, stroed in it, of every face that the person knows
The brain compares the input face with each of its stored templates for faces
The template with the highest similarity to the input face is what is perceived
If there’s a name associated with the winning template, that name is the perceptual decision 
What this theory implies for AI: The knowledge weights of NNs are like perceptual templates. 
Remmber this from before: So the NN combines its currrent weights with the input face pixels and produces a Computed Output that is wrong (when we haven’t learnt anything)!
So the way that an NN’s weights/knowledge/templates are combined with the input is that we determine similarity between weights and inputs.
This is difficult to understand now, but just keep this in mind.
Hierarchical Perception

For a long time, psychologists and neuroscientists have known that perception is done in stages, hierarchically
So the input leads to one new representation, then that representation becomes another, then another, till the output decision is made!

NNs are Templatic Hierarchical Perceivers

Let’s first talk about the templatic aspect
The key to templatic perception is that some internal template of numbers is compared to some input set of numbers to find out how similar the template is to the input
NNs assume: Input is a list or vector of numbers and internal template weights are also a list or vector of numbers
So how can we compare two lists of numbers to determine if they are similar or not.
E.g.
Input = [-1  3  -2]
Temp1 = [-2  0  3]
Temp2  = [-2   2  -1]
Is list Input more similar to template 1 or 2?
Inner product: 
Multiply 2 lists component-wise
Add all products
If IP is near 0, the lists are dissimilar
If IP is large and positive, lists are similar
Neural Networks

Inference: We give the system a signal vector, the w’s are inner producted (template matching) over and over again (hierarchical perception) like Euler’s algorithm 
Learning: We give the system a signal a vector whose identity we know, we ask it to infer its identity, with initial random w’s. It can’t. So the w’s are improved via SGD!
